sentences.text: This appeal by the insurance company under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 15.09.2023 passed by IInd MACT, Indore in claim case no.1610/2021 seeking reduction of the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the claims tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the tribunal, for the death of Banshilal @ Banshi Tanwar, the tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.40,68,300/- along with interest from the date of claim petition till its realization.

3. Counsel for the appellant/insurance company submits that tribunal has grossly erred in not considering the income tax record of the deceased in which it has been found that the deceased had produced income tax return for the assessment year 2019-20 Rs.3,30,790/-.
Further it is to be noted that income tax return of assessment year 2019-20 has been produced in which his income has been mentioned till 31st March, 2019 and accident had occurred on 30.06.2020.

As the deceased had not produced any income tax return for the assessment year 2020-21 and only produced the income tax return till the assessment year 2019-20 which shows that he was earning Rs.3,30,790/- till 31st March, 2019.
Hence, there is no production of documents by the deceased regarding what he was earning from 31st March, 2019 till 30.06.2020.
Therefore, how his income of Rs.3,30,790/- which he was earning till 31st March, 2019 can be considered as his income in the next year also.
There may be a possible situation that he would had suffered business loss.
So the tribunal has committed error in assessing the income of the deceased by by considering the income tax return for the assessment year 2019-20.

In support of his contention he has placed reliance over the decision of this court in the case of Harvindar Kaur vs. M/s Motor Transport of India) MA No.1823/2003 decided on 09.11.2012.
4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, respondents/claimants have filed a cross objection (DOC No.1873/24) and submits that tribunal has committed error in deducting 1/3rd amount towards personal expenses instead of 1/4th amount because all the three children of the deceased are students and are not earning members.
5. Learned counsel for both parties prayed for dismissal of the appeal as well as cross objection of each other.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

sentences.text:
After going through the record it is found that before the tribunal the claimants have filed income tax returns Ex.P/13, P/14, P/15 & P/16 for the assessment years 2016-17, 2017-18, 21018-19 &
2019-2020.
It is true that claimants have not filed the income tax return for the assessment year 2020-21.
The deceased died on 30.06.2020.
Perusal of income tax return for the assessment year 2019-20 it is found that the income of the deceased was mentioned from 1st April, 2018 to 31st March, 2019.

Learned counsel for the insurance company submits that claimants are unable to produce income tax return for the assessment year 2020-21 and relied upon the decision in the case of Harvindar Kaur (supra) in which the claimants have filed only one income tax return.
But in the present case the claimants have filed Ex.P/13 to P/16, income tax returns from assessment years 2016 1-17 to 2019-20.
Perusal of the income tax returns Ex.P/13 to P/16 it is found that the income of the deceased was increased year by year.

Learned counsel for the insurance company submits that it may be possible that income of deceased may be decreased but it is the duty of the insurance company to prove that income of the deceased was decreased in year 2020-21 but the insurance company has unable to prove that.
So mere presumption cannot be treated as a basis for decrease of the income of the deceased for the assessment year 2020-21.
8. Perusal of para-25 & 26 of the impugned award, in the considered opinion of this Court, the tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the deceased on the basis of the income tax returns Ex.P/16.
So there is no need to interfere in the said finding of the tribunal .
So in view of the aforesaid discussion, there is no need to interfere in this regard in the award.
Accordingly, the appeal filed by the insurance company has no substance and is hereby dismissed.

9. So far as the cross objection filed by the claimants is concerned seeking enhancement of compensation, it is found that the tribunal has committed an error in deducting 1/3rd amount towards personal expenses.
Perusal of the award it is found that the claimant no.1 is the wife of the deceased and no.2, 3 & 4 are sons of the deceased and they are students.
So in the considered opinion of this court, they were dependents upon the deceased at the time of accident.

In the case of Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation - (2009) 6 SCC 121 the apex Court has held that if the dependents are 4 to 6, 1/4th amount should be deducted towards personal and living expenses.

entities.text: Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation - (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the tribunal has committed an error in deducting 1/3rd amount towards personal expenses in the present case.
Accordingly, the finding of the tribunal in this regard is modified as aforesaid.

Thus, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is recalculated as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT  Loss of dependency -Rs.43,41,624/-
(i.e. Rs.3,30,790 25% FP=4,13,487 - 1/4 PE=310116 x 14(m)) Consortium -Rs.1,76,000/-
 Funeral expenses -Rs.16,500/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.16,500/-
 ----------------
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.45,50,624/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.40,68,212/-.

Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Santosh on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146121395/
3 additional sum of Rs.4,82,412/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
11.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the result, the cross objection filed by the claimants is allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.4,82,412/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
The claimants have valued the cross objection only to the extent of Rs.1 lakh and paid the Court fee accordingly.

However, for the remaining amount, the Court fee shall be paid by the claimants within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months, the claimants shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
12. In the result, the appeal filed by the insurance company is dismissed whereas the cross objection filed by the claimants is allowed to the extent indicated herein above.
